headlines.title: 16-year-old lifeguard makes daring first rescue, earns White House invite
headlines.description: Despite forecasts predicting rip currents and sneaker waves, people still headed to the beach as the summer winds down. Conditions are similar to what they were one week ago when a teenage lifeguard rushed into the pounding surf to rescue a 10-year-old boy. His name is Ryder Williams, and he is just 16. You wouldn’t know it by watching the video of the rescue, but this is his first season as a lifeguard, and this was his very first rescue. Facing 8- to 10-foot-high pounding surf, sneaker waves and rip currents at Seabright Beach last week in Santa Cruz, Williams sprinted into the potentially deadly conditions. “I look up and see a young boy get swept off his feet from a low point on the beach, and I started running up the beach as he gets pulled out,” Williams said. He grabbed onto 10-year-old Nathaniel Rai and never let go, even as they were both slammed over and over again by unrelenting waves. Williams described what was going through his mind during his fight against the powerful surf. “As I grab the child, he goes limp. I’m thinking is he unconscious or not … the whole time I just need to hold my position ’til my partner can get there,” Williams said. Another lifeguard and others on the beach jumped in to help. Nathaniel’s father, Sumit Rai, said his son was unconscious during the rescue and that he is forever grateful for the young lifeguard’s courage and resilience. “He risked his life to save my child going into that water and those tumultuous conditions and getting thrown under is incredibly dangerous,” Sumit Rai said. Rai added that words cannot fully express his gratitude. “It’s incredibly courageous, brave, heroic and resilient. Had he let go of him, this would have been a different outcome,” Rai said. When Williams pulled Nathaniel onto the beach, he completed his first rescue as a lifeguard, but it was not his last that day. “I returned to the tower and ended up making more rescues later that day,” Williams said. He went on to make four additional rescues in conditions he said were even more challenging than the life-saving measures he took to save Nathaniel. Video of the rescue captivated people around the nation and the world, including President Donald Trump, who called the young man “heroic.” On social media, the president said he plans to invite Williams and his family to the White House to receive a high civilian honor.

headlines.title: Fire sparks at the former Kaiser Estate in Lafayette
headlines.description: A fire broke out at the former Kaiser Estate in Lafayette on Saturday, according to the Contra Costa County Fire Department. The fire department said just before 7 p.m. that crews responded to a third-alarm fire at the former Kaiser Estate at 940 Reliez Station Lane in Lafayette. No injuries have been reported and officials said nobody was in the residence.

headlines.title: Forward Progress Stopped on 841-Acre Feliz Fire in Mendocino County
headlines.description: A fast-moving wildfire near Hopland triggered evacuation orders Saturday, forcing Mendocino County residents from their homes and impacting travel along Highway 101. The Feliz Fire, burning near Feliz Creek Road, has reached 841 acres and is 10% contained as of Sunday morning. The fire’s forward progress has been successfully stopped, though mandatory evacuation orders remain in effect, according to Cal Fire. Evacuation Zones and Traffic: — Evacuation Orders: Zones MEN-2HOP04 and MEN-2UKV29. — Evacuation Warnings: Downtown Hopland and zones MEN-2HOP01, MEN-2UKV20, MEN-2UKV21 and MEN-2UKV23. — Highway 101 remains open with traffic control in place. Officials urge all drivers to use caution in the area. Local authorities have established multiple locations to assist displaced residents and their animals: — Temporary Evacuation Point: Mendocino County Office of Education, 2240 Old River Road, Ukiah. — Evacuation Shelter: Coyote Valley Tribal Gymnasium, 415 Coyote Valley Blvd., Redwood Valley. — Small Animal Shelter: 298 Plant Road, Ukiah. — Large Animal Shelter: Redwood Empire Fairgrounds, 1055 N. State St., Ukiah. A map of evacuation orders and warning can be seen at http://nbcbay.com/OU7ANev. No injuries have been reported.

headlines.title: Body found on Caltrain platform in San Francisco
headlines.description: The body of a deceased man was found on a Caltrain platform in San Francisco Saturday morning, according to the police department. Police said officers responded to the Caltrain platform on the 1100 block of 22nd Street at around 8:06 a.m. regarding a report of a deceased person. At the scene, officials said paramedics declared the man deceased and the Medical Examiner arrived to conduct an investigation. The police department asks anyone with information to contact the SFPD at 415-575-4444 or Text a Tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD.

headlines.title: Grieving aunt hosts anual backpack giveway to honor another loved one in Oakland
headlines.description: The aunt of the woman killed in an Oakland shooting on Friday hosted a community event on Saturday that honors another family member and helps the community. Just 24 hours after the shooting that killed 25-year-old Kimarrii McLemore, her aunt Brittia Johnson showed up with a heavy heart to host her anual event honoring Johnson’s daughter, Euniece Law, who was killed on May 28, 2007. With the new school year around the corner, the event includes backpacks, a resource fair, a car show and more. Despite these recent events, Johnson showed up to the event to honor her late daughter and niece. “That just says a lot to her character that even through everything that she is going through that she is still feels she should be here for the community that’s really appreciated,” Chanel of Oakland said. Johnson urges community members to “put down the guns,” regarding the shooting from Friday night. The police are still searching for the suspect from the shooting.

headlines.title: Human remains, including those of a baby, found in 2 locations in Monterey County
headlines.description: The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said they are investigating two separate incidents of human remains, including those of a baby, found in two different locations on Saturday. Just after 8:30 a.m., Fire/EMS and sheriff’s deputies were dispatched to a report of an infant that had been located near the 100 block of Struve Road, near Moss Landing, in north Monterey County, according to authorities. Officials said the fire personnel confirmed the infant was deceased. More than an hour later, at around 9:55 a.m., deputies went to the 400 block of Old Stage Road in Salinas after a county employee found what appeared to be human remains, according to the sheriff’s office. The sheriff’s office said both of these incidents are being actively investigated. They ask anyone with information related to either of them to contact them at 831-755-3700.

headlines.title: Firefighters battle vegetation fire in the South Bay
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a fire in the South Bay Saturday. Cal Fire said crews were battling a half-acre near Hicks Road and Mount Umunhum Road, close to South San Jose. The fire was spreading slow and crews have already sprayed retardant and were making good progress, according to officials. Cal Fire said no structures were threatened and no injuries have been reported so far. This is a developing story.

headlines.title: Top dogs ride waves at annual World Dog Surfing Championships
headlines.description: Top dogs were riding waves Saturday at the annual World Dog Surfing Championships as hundreds of spectators cheered — and barked — from the Northern California beach. From small spaniels to large labs, the canines were judged on factors including how long they could stay on their board, the size of the wave and their confidence. In its 10th year, the contest in Pacifica, about 14 miles (22 kilometers) south of San Francisco, includes a pet adoption event and fundraising for local animal charities. The dogs, sporting their colorful life vests, stood ready on their surfboards and were assisted by human participants, who spotted the best wave to carry the board to the beach. Spectators erupted in applause and cheered with each successful ride. A dog catches a wave during the World Dog Surfing Championships, Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026, in Pacifica, Calif. Sophia Sadlowski first put her Miniature Pinscher, Rusty, on her surfboard to capture fun photos when he was just a puppy. “And then … he didn’t want to get off,” said Sadlowski, of Huntington Beach, California. “I walk over to the beach, and I put him on a wave, and he surfed it.” Small-, medium- and large- sized dogs competed in heats and then the highest scoring dogs in each heat faced off for the top prize. The day also included tandem contests, where multiple dogs, as well as dogs and humans, shared the surfboard. Rusty’s life jacket was green with animal print and a shark fin sticking up out of his back and his goggles gave the impression he was a fierce competitor for the small-sized and tandem dog competitions. Sadlowski said Rusty was in his first surf competition at four months old, and she and her pup are now both cancer-free. “He was four months old, and he took third place. So we’ve been surfing since,” Sadlowski said. “We got hooked.” Diet & Exercise Jul 29 Pets Jul 10 clear the shelters Jul 22 Chicago animal rescue plans 20-acre ranch to help homeless pets at risk of euthanasia

headlines.title: Series of earthquakes strike near Cloverdale
headlines.description: A series of earthquakes struck near Cloverdale on Saturday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The first was a 3.8 magnitude earthquake that hit at 12:57 a.m., 4.7 miles east-southeast of Cloverdale. The second one, a 2.8 magnitude quake, hit hours later at 4:35 a.m., 4.4 miles east-southeast of Cloverdale. It was followed by a 2.7 quake that hit at 4:50 a.m., 4.8 miles east-southeast of Cloverdale. headlines.title: San Francisco Ghirardelli workers enter final day of strike
headlines.description: Multiple Ghirardelli employees entered the final day of their three-day strike in San Francisco. The Original Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Store in Ghirardelli Square, San Francisco, closed on Thursday after its employees began their three day strike. The strike was organized by UNITE HERE Local 2, who says workers are accusing the company of failing to disclose how much revenue is generated from a 6% healthcare surcharge charged to customers. The employees are also protesting for changes to their healthcare coverage. According to the union, the shop has reopened using temporary replacement workers. Ghirardelli says it “values and respects” its employees and is engaged in active contract negotiations. Picketing is expected to continue through Saturday night at the Original Ghirardelli Ice Cream & Chocolate Store.

headlines.title: 3 arrested in connection with shooting in Santa Cruz
headlines.description: Three people have been arrested in connection with a July 13 shooting in Santa Cruz that investigators believe may be gang-related, police said Friday. The Santa Cruz Police Department announced that detectives served search warrants in Santa Cruz and Watsonville as part of the ongoing investigation into the shooting in the 500 block of Errett Circle. Jose Ernesto Puga Banuelos was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, assault with a firearm, discharging a firearm at an occupied vehicle, and conspiracy. Guadalupe Manuel Figueroa Escoto was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder, assault with a firearm, and discharging a firearm at an occupied vehicle. Anthony Jose Sanchez-Escobar was arrested on suspicion of carrying a loaded firearm in public. Police said officers responded to reports of gunfire at about 8:07 p.m. July 13 and found evidence of a shooting, but no injuries were reported. Investigators believe the incident may be gang related. The investigation remains active, and anyone with information is asked to contact the Santa Cruz Police Department or submit an anonymous tip through the department’s tip line at (831) 420- 5995.

headlines.title: Vegetation fire in Oakland Hills leaves neighbors on edge
headlines.description: As fire crews across the Bay Area prepare for a hot weekend and elevated fire danger, dozens of firefighters were called to a well-known park in the Oakland Hills to fight a vegetation fire. Flames ripped through dry brushes just off the Sequoia Bay Hiking Trail, sending smoke rising above the Oakland Hills. It started just before 7 p.m. Friday, prompting a rapid response from Oakland Fire, with help from Contra Costa Fire and Cal Fire, to surround the flames before they could spread. “Crews did a phenomenal job getting to the location of the fire and then allocating crews to make sure we extinguish it as quickly as possible,” Michael Hunt with Oakland Fire said. That quick response stopped the fire at just over half an acre in less than an hour. And that speed mattered. The dense vegetation and tall trees inside Joaquin Miller Park can make firefighting challenging, especially as fire danger begins to increase across the region. “The size of the trees and dense vegetation in the area makes it not only a really complex response but also one that requires us to be extremely efficient and quick to get to contain and stop forward progress,” Hunt said. “That’s actually what got us out of the house. We saw the planes circling, so loaded the kids up to see what was going on,” Oakland resident Josh Lynch said. For people who live in the Oakland Hills, a fire like this can be especially unnerving. The 1991 Oakland Hills firestorm also began as a small grass fire before strong winds reignited it the next day, killing 25 people and destroying more than 3,000 homes. That history is why even a half-acre fire can put neighbors on edge. The Lynch family says they were relieved to learn this fire was stopped quickly but admit their first thought was whether they might have to evacuate. “I just had that thought before we left the house. I hope we don’t need to evacuate. I actually have everything prepared in a situation like that,” Angeli Lynch said. Firefighters will remain in the area overnight, searching for hot spots and cutting away vegetation to make sure this fire doesn’t flare back up as warmer, drier conditions move into the Bay Area. No structures were threatened and there are no reports of any injuries.
